It was a really smart match 3, for two reasons (3, I found another one):

  1. Consistent ratio of pieces ensures you always have at least one match you can do, even if it's of a match that can hurt you, but planning (pt 2, below) should eliminate the possibility but you can still progress. Other match 3s don't take this into consideration and instead "mix" the board when there's no possible matches because of bad ratio, randomization and "bad" pieces that people leave behind and try not to use and are forced into using if they plan wrong. This is the same sort of concept as when The Tetris Company instituted the random generator that is standardized across official Tetris games, enabling "infinite" play for the player that makes the right calls.

  2. Generally with a match 3 you're limited to matching icons that are immediately next to each other, Bejeweled and Candy Crush follow this philosophy, this is because of the limit of the input device; controllers, touch screens, which makes the "randomize game board if no move" mechanic necessary. What sets HuniePop apart is the ability to, instead of immediately connect a match shifting only one additional piece out of the way, you can choose any piece within a row or column to shift in order to "push" it so that you can plan out future moves, controlling the entirety of the board if you plan far enough ahead and take the ratio of pieces (8 per icon without modifier) into consideration to know roughly what and where a piece can be put.

  3. The mechanics of how to win can be changed depending on modifier; you can have your passion or your sentiment dumped to fill your meter and you can plan strategies around that instead of focusing on simple matches, or building infinite play with a modifier that gives you a free move every time you make a 4x or higher match, and planning to do only those can turn 20 moves into 50+

Anyway, it's pretty cerebral for a match 3. They did a great job on it which is why it's a little frustrating when people say it's "only" a match 3 game.
